reason: Confirmed by driving ?v=dark&state=full in chromium at 1440x960 and reading computed style off the live nodes. The mechanism is exactly as described: lately.html:645-649 hard-codes stroke="#d97706" / "#ef4444" / "#4f46e5" / "#059669" on the four status glyphs, while ICON.up and ICON.down two lines above (640-641) already use stroke="currentColor" — so the file contains both patterns and the status four are the ones that missed. In dark the four .kpi .glyph shapes computed to rgb(217,119,6), rgb(239,68,68), rgb(79,70,229), rgb(5,150,105) — byte-identical to light, confirming they do not take the ground flip, while --accent resolves to #818cf8 and every other indigo mark on the surface (12 var(--accent) uses: live column, meter fills, hatch, dots, focus ring) does. The plate is real: .glyph background is --wash = rgba(255,255,255,0.04) over .kpi background --paper = rgb(24,24,27), compositing to #212124 (the finding says #202023; one rounding step off, immaterial). Indigo 600 on that plate is 2.55:1 — the finding's 2.58 is what you get on #202023, so its own number is right to two figures — against a 3:1 floor for a meaning-carrying mark. The sharpest version of the claim is one the seat only implies: in that same card the meter directly beneath the square computes to rgb(129,140,248), so the 'has nobody's name on it' card paints Indigo 600 and Indigo 400 forty pixels apart, in a twin whose written rule (lately.html:86-90) is that indigo steps to 400 because 600 on near-black reads as a bruise. That is a self-contradiction in the file, measured, not taste. The gate claim is right in effect and imprecise in mechanism: audit.mjs DOES walk fill/stroke — colorProps at line 200 includes both and paints() at 197 gates them on el.matches(SHAPES) — but only for the palette lock; the contrast block fires solely on hasText/::placeholder, so no non-text mark on this surface is contrast-checked. Nothing sees it, for a different reason than stated. Two corrections that do not change the verdict. (1) The neighbour ratios 5.6/4.7/4.7 are measured against #18181b, not against the wash plate the finding itself argues is the right backdrop; on that plate they are 5.04/4.27/4.27. The outlier gap holds either way. (2) 'a row that should read as four distinct kinds of slippage reads as three plus a blank' is overstated — captured at deviceScaleFactor 3 and compared against a patched twin, the square is plainly visible, just muddier and a step darker than every other indigo on the page. Defect is the right class and I am keeping it: visibly wrong, passable, nothing asserted untrue and nothing broken. The proposed fix is mechanically correct and I verified it: setting color on .glyph and stroke="currentColor" on the shapes moved the square to rgb(129,140,248) (5.38:1 on the plate) and left the amber circle at rgb(217,119,6) untouched. Light is a genuine no-op because --accent is #4f46e5 in :root and --amber/--red/--emerald carry no dark override at all. No new hue, no new weight, no architecture touched.
sharpenedFix: Take the proposed fix with one addition it omits. ICON.clear (lately.html:649) is a fifth glyph in the same object, rendered into a bare .glyph in the quiet state at line 924. If it is converted to currentColor along with its four siblings but its wrapper is not given a tone, it inherits color from the card — #ffffff in dark — and the emerald tick silently becomes a white tick. So either leave clear hard-coded (works, but leaves the file with two conventions for one object) or, better, convert all five and give the quiet card's glyph the emerald tone too. Plumbing: kpi() takes glyph as an opaque HTML string, so pass a tone alongside it and emit style="color:var(--amber|--red|--accent|--emerald)" on the span; do not add a new token — all four already exist and only --accent is redefined in dark, which is precisely the one that should move. While in here, note a separate defect the fix will put you nose-to-nose with and should not silently fix: the comment at lately.html:642-644 states the order is 'amber, indigo, red, emerald ... because red adjacent to amber fails CVD separation at 4.4', but the row is rendered still/past/nobody/waiting at lines 813-816, i.e. amber, red, indigo, emerald — red IS adjacent to amber. The code and its own stated CVD rationale disagree. That belongs in its own finding.
breaks: Low blast radius, three things to re-measure. (1) audit.mjs palette lock now reads the glyph strokes as computed colours rather than authored hexes: in dark the nobody square resolves to rgb(129,140,248) = Indigo 400, which is in the locked 18, so it should pass — but run the gate on both grounds and all seven states, because this is the first non-text mark on the surface whose computed colour is variant-dependent. (2) The loading state is safe by construction — .sk-wrap svg { visibility: hidden } at line 460 — but re-shoot it anyway, since .sk-wrap .glyph { background: var(--wash) } at 457 now sits under a coloured, not a fixed, stroke. (3) Re-shoot dark full, quiet and partial: quiet is the one that regresses if ICON.clear is converted without a tone, and partial renders the past card in its unavailable form, where the glyph paints beside an em dash rather than a numeral. interaction-check.mjs asserts nothing about glyph colour, so it should be untouched; run it to confirm the 366 assertions still hold rather than assuming it.
